name: RTMDet (CSPNeXt, tiny / S / M / L / X; nano and M person detectors)
plain: OpenMMLab's RTMDet (tiny, s, m, l, x on COCO; nano and m person detectors): real-time one-stage box detector, a CSPNeXt CNN with NMS. The person detectors supply the boxes for RTMPose. Apache-2.0.
summary: RTMDet (Lyu et al. 2022, OpenMMLab): real-time one-stage detector, all convolutions: a CSPNeXt backbone (5 x 5 depthwise convs), a CSPNeXt-PAFPN neck and a head that predicts, per cell of the stride 8 / 16 / 32 maps, a score per class and the distances to the four box edges; class-wise NMS. COCO checkpoints (80 classes) from mmdetection and the person-only detectors mmpose ships as the box source of RTMPose (same backbone family as `fastforks.pose`'s RTMPose). The image is fitted into 640 x 640 (nano: 320 x 320); vendored from mmdetection (no mmdet / mmcv dependency). The portable `module()` is the whole network (class logits and decoded boxes per cell, before NMS).

papers.title: RTMDet: An Empirical Study of Designing Real-Time Object Detectors

limitations: The image is resized like OpenCV 4's 8-bit INTER_LINEAR (what mmdetection calls); OpenCV 5 resizes differently by up to two grey levels, so a reference run on OpenCV 5 differs slightly.
Boxes are not clamped to the image, as upstream: at the right or bottom border they can reach a few pixels into the padding.
The person detectors' released config names COCO only; the training config stored in the checkpoints (and the file name) also lists Objects365.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: boxes, class labels, scores and instance masks.
